newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Chechen commanders put pressure on president.
newsitem.headline: Chechen commanders put pressure on president.

text.p: Independent-minded field commanders in the Russian rebel region of Chechnya threw down a challenge to their president on Sunday by urging him to form an armed group to free Chechen hostages held in a neighbouring region.

But Chechen President Aslan Maskhadov, who needs to show he has control over the commanders to strengthen his hand in tough negotiations with the Kremlin, made clear he was not prepared to back a violent solution.
Five Chechens were seized on July 8 in neighbouring North Ossetia by abductors who hoped to swap them for relatives held hostage in Chechnya. By Sunday, three of the Chechens had been freed.

The field commanders said in a resolution read out after a meeting in the Chechen capital, Grozny, that the armed group could also be used to avenge any future attacks on Chechens elsewhere in the world.
Chechen vice-president Vakha Arsanov and deputy premier Movladi Udugov attended the meeting but Maskhadov, a pragmatist who overcame more hardline rivals in an election in January, did not.
The field commanders gained influence during 21 months of resistance to Russia's attempt to subdue Chechnya's independence bid, which ended in a peace deal last August.
But Maskhadov, who says he still wants full independence for Chechnya, is now involved in complex talks with the Kremlin and needs stability to boost his negotiating position.
He has said any attempt to free Chechens in North Ossetia must conform to the peace deal with Russia under which the sides promised not to solve problems by force.
He told a news conference in Grozny that a military operation in North Ossetia could drag Chechnya into another conflict in the volatile North Caucasus, adding: "We will not allow this."

Hostage-taking has become a huge problem in and around Chechnya, where six Russian journalists, two Britons, one Frenchman and a Slovak have been among the dozens of people abducted. But there have been no other reports of Chechens being seized elsewhere.
Interfax news agency quoted Maskhadov as saying earlier on Sunday that a special group of 300 fighters with extensive powers had been set up to seek and free hostages held in Chechnya.
